counterfactual_missing_items: Transthoracic echocardiography showed no valvular vegetations
decisive_items: Repeat lumbar puncture showed an opening pressure of 30 cm H₂O, 1762 WBCs/mm³ (60% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 123 mg/dL, glucose 30 mg/dL (serum 105 mg/dL), and no red cells.
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement.

Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³ (57% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 81 mg/dL, and glucose 57 mg/dL (serum 121 mg/dL); Gram stain was negative.
response.rationale: R7 is the best fit: purulent CSF with neutrophilic pleocytosis, low glucose, and elevated protein, plus progression to necrosis and peripheral enhancement, strongly favor pyogenic brain abscess in an IV drug user. R1 is the closest alternative because basal ganglia mass effect and restricted diffusion can occur in toxoplasmosis, but initial lack of enhancement and negative protozoal investigations make it secondary. PML, vasculitis, rickettsial infection, and endocarditis are excluded by negative JCV PCR, negative rickettsial studies, non-vasculitic CSF, and absent valvular vegetations.

rejected.why: No valvular vegetations on echocardiography; the CSF and MRI evolution point to a parenchymal abscess rather than endocarditis.
Purulent CSF with low glucose and progression to necrosis/ring enhancement are not a vasculitic pattern.
Negative JCV PCR, fever, neutrophilic CSF, and progressive enhancement/necrosis are incompatible with PML.
Appending negative JCV PCR to PML does not rescue the diagnosis and is self-contradictory.
Rickettsial studies were negative, and the CSF profile and imaging evolution favor pyogenic abscess.
